answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using transitive credit networks, routing transactions along an interconnected vine of bilateral trust. Nodes settle payments via mutual credit, forcing an attacker to incur the scarce cost of genuine counterparty underwriting per identity. Graph bottlenecks reduce malicious propagation to the crawl of a glacier, driving Sybil influence to a nadir. However, this model limits liquidity and penalizes honest newcomers lacking established credit.
